tasks.behavior: One chain whose RPC hosts are down no longer stops the api, worker and signer: that chain waits until two hosts answer again, and the other chains keep working
acceptance: When an enabled chain's RPC hosts don't answer at startup (fewer than two answer), the api, worker and signer log that chain as unavailable and start, as they already keep running through an outage; nothing is decided paid or settled without the second RPC (D-15), as before. Both roles are asked at once, so a role is checked even when the other is down

A mistake in the chain list or on chain still stops them: a chain missing from the list, a chain listing one host, a role whose hosts all serve another chain, no factory code, or an executor without gas
The startup factory check (address.FactoryDeployed) and the signer's gas check (settlement.CheckGas) ask the second RPC when the primary fails, instead of stopping on the primary's error
unit passes

tasks.behavior: A host whose endpoints hang no longer holds its RPC role: when one endpoint of a host times out or can't connect, the whole host rests, so calls reach the role's next host
acceptance: When an endpoint times out or fails to connect, every endpoint of its host rests, so a call reaches the role's next host after one AttemptTimeout instead of cycling through the host's other keys (today several hanging Infura keys hold the role, since each rests less than an attempt takes)
A failure of one key (HTTP 401 or a rate limit) still rests only that key
